mainTopic: Whether מעשר שני and קדשים קלים may be eaten without a standing בית המקדש or מזבח, and the debate over רבי ישמעאל's proof.
overview: The amud opens with a teaching of רבי ישמעאל, one of 'three elders.' He asks whether מעשר שני may be eaten in ירושלים today, without the בית המקדש. Comparisons to בכור and to ביכורים are each knocked down, and even a מה הצד fails because both share צד מזבח. So he proves from a פסוק that links מעשר to בכור that מעשר is eaten only while the בית המקדש stands. The גמרא then asks what רבי ישמעאל holds about קדושה ראשונה. רבינא explains that the case is a בכור whose blood was sprinkled before the חורבן: its meat is tied to its blood and needs a מזבח, and מעשר learns from it. The גמרא defends this chain against the rule that one היקש cannot teach through another, ending with the idea that blood and meat count as one thing. Then רבין brings this rule to ארץ ישראל, and רבי ירמיה rejects it using two ברייתות about the מדבר journeys. רבינא begins to answer that both ברייתות speak about קדשים קלים, and his explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Can second tithe be eaten in Jerusalem today?
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל raises the question of whether מעשר שני may be brought to ירושלים and eaten after the בית המקדש is gone.
steps.simpleTranslation: Three elders, and this is one of them: רבי ישמעאל says: You might think a person could bring מעשר שני up to ירושלים and eat it nowadays.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא introduces a teaching of רבי ישמעאל, and he opens with a 'you might think' question. This sets up the discussion that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word יכול signals a possible mistaken idea that the teaching will go on to reject. The question is whether eating מעשר שני in ירושלים depends on the בית המקדש standing, or only on the city.

keyTerms.meaning: Three elders: this teaching is presented as one of three
'You might think': it introduces an idea that will be rejected
Second tithe: produce that must be eaten in ירושלים
Nowadays, when there is no בית המקדש

phrases.english: Three elders, and this is one of them:
Rabbi Yishmael says:

phrases.aramaic: יָכוֹל יַעֲלֶה אָדָם מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי לִירוּשָׁלַיִם
phrases.english: One might think a person may bring second tithe up to Jerusalem
and eat it in the present time?
phrases.notes: He means after the בית המקדש was destroyed.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל יַעֲלֶה אָדָם מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי לִירוּשָׁלַיִם
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does eating מעשר שני in ירושלים require the בית המקדש to be standing?

steps.title: A logical comparison to the firstborn
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל proposes a דין: מעשר and בכור both must be brought to the holy place, so מעשר should work only while the בית המקדש stands, like בכור.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it could be proven by logic: בכור must be brought to the place, and מעשר must be brought to the place. Just as בכור applies only while the בית המקדש stands, so too מעשר applies only while the בית המקדש stands.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ישמעאל tries to answer his question with a logical comparison between מעשר שני and בכור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The shared feature is that both must be brought to ירושלים. Since בכור clearly needs the בית המקדש, he argues that מעשר should need it too.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And it is logical': this introduces a proof from reasoning
A firstborn animal, brought as a קרבן
Being brought to the chosen place, ירושלים
While the בית המקדש stands

phrases.english: And it is a logical inference:
A firstborn requires bringing to the place,
and tithe requires bringing to the place;

phrases.aramaic: מָה בְּכוֹר – אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא בִּפְנֵי הַבַּיִת,
phrases.english: just as a firstborn is only in the presence of the Temple,

phrases.aramaic: אַף מַעֲשֵׂר – אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא בִּפְנֵי הַבַּיִת.
phrases.english: so too tithe is only in the presence of the Temple.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a first answer to the question in step 1.
steps.raayaObject: מעשר שני is eaten only while the בית המקדש stands.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A logical comparison to בכור, since both must be brought to the holy place.

steps.title: The firstborn is different: it goes on the altar
steps.stepSummary: The comparison is challenged: בכור has blood and parts offered on the מזבח, which מעשר does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: What about בכור? It is special, because it requires putting its blood and parts on the מזבח!
steps.whatsHappening: The logical comparison from step 2 is attacked. בכור has a special feature that מעשר lacks.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Maybe בכור needs the בית המקדש only because it needs a working מזבח for its blood and אימורים. מעשר שני is only eaten, so it might not need the בית המקדש at all.

keyTerms.meaning: 'What about...?': it points out that the two cases are different
Putting blood on the מזבח
Parts of a קרבן that are burned on the מזבח

phrases.english: What about a firstborn? It is notable in that it requires
placing blood and sacrificial portions on the altar!

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה לִבְכוֹר, שֶׁכֵּן טָעוּן מַתַּן דָּמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the logical proof in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The comparison of מעשר to בכור.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: בכור's need for the בית המקדש may come from its מזבח service, which מעשר does not have.

steps.title: First fruits prove the point
steps.stepSummary: ביכורים have no blood on the מזבח, yet they still need the בית המקדש. So the מזבח feature is not what matters.
steps.whatsHappening: The argument is defended by bringing a different example, ביכורים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ביכורים must be brought to ירושלים, have no blood or אימורים, and still apply only while the בית המקדש stands. This shows that being 'brought to the place' alone can make something depend on the בית המקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: First fruits brought to the בית המקדש
'Will prove': a counter-example that answers the challenge

phrases.english: First fruits will prove it.
phrases.notes: First fruits are also brought to ירושלים only while the בית המקדש stands, even though no blood is involved.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only things with blood on the מזבח need the בית המקדש.
steps.terutzMaskana: ביכורים have no blood and still need the בית המקדש, so the מזבח feature is not the reason.

steps.title: First fruits are different: they are placed by the altar
steps.stepSummary: ביכורים are challenged too: they must be set down next to the מזבח, which מעשר does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: What about ביכורים? They are special, because they require being placed down by the מזבח!
steps.whatsHappening: The new example from step 4 is attacked, because ביכורים also have a special feature.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ביכורים need the מזבח for הנחה, so they too may need the בית המקדש only for that reason. מעשר שני has no מזבח connection at all, so neither example proves anything about it. The logical approach fails.

keyTerms.meaning: Setting the ביכורים down next to the מזבח
'Since it...': it points to the special feature

phrases.english: What about first fruits? They are notable in that they require placement!
phrases.notes: He means placing them down beside the מזבח.

steps.kashyaAttackLogic: ביכורים also involve the מזבח (through הנחה), so they cannot show that something with no מזבח connection, like מעשר, needs the בית המקדש.

steps.title: A verse links tithe to the firstborn
steps.stepSummary: Since logic failed, רבי ישמעאל uses a פסוק that lists מעשר and בכור together. This היקש proves that מעשר is eaten only while the בית המקדש stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'And there you shall bring your burnt offerings...' It links מעשר to בכור. Just as בכור applies only while the בית המקדש stands, so too מעשר applies only while the בית המקדש stands.
steps.whatsHappening: Logic could not settle the question, so רבי ישמעאל proves the answer from a פסוק. The same conclusion line from step 2 is repeated, but now it rests on a firm source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An היקש from the תורה does not depend on finding identical features, so the challenges from steps 3 and 5 no longer matter. The final rule is that מעשר שני may not be eaten in ירושלים nowadays.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The פסוק teaches': it introduces a proof from a verse
Links two things together so that they share the same law (היקש)
'Etc.': the rest of the פסוק

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי ישמעאל, מעשר שני is eaten in ירושלים only while the בית המקדש stands. This comes from an היקש to בכור, because the logical comparisons (בכור, then ביכורים) were each challenged.
steps.confusionAlert: The last line looks the same as the line in step 2, but it is not a repeat of the failed logic. Now the conclusion rests on a פסוק, not on reasoning.

phrases.english: Therefore the verse states:
'And there you shall bring your burnt offerings, etc.'
It juxtaposes tithe with the firstborn;

phrases.aramaic: מָה בְּכוֹר – אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא בִּפְנֵי הַבַּיִת,
phrases.english: just as a firstborn is only in the presence of the Temple,

phrases.aramaic: אַף מַעֲשֵׂר – אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא בִּפְנֵי הַבַּיִת.
phrases.english: so too tithe is only in the presence of the Temple.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the logical proofs fail (steps 3 and 5), it proves the rule from a פסוק.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: מעשר שני is eaten in ירושלים only while the בית המקדש stands. This is learned from an היקש to בכור in דברים 12:6.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that, for רבי ישמעאל, eating מעשר שני depends on the בית המקדש itself and not just on the city of ירושלים.

steps.title: Why not combine בכור and ביכורים in a מה הצד?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי ישמעאל needed a פסוק. He could have used both earlier sources together in a מה הצד argument.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let the logic come back around, and let us learn it through a 'מה הצד' (what they have in common)!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges step 6. Why use a פסוק when logic could still work by joining בכור and ביכורים together?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each source alone was knocked down by its own special feature: בכור has blood on the מזבח, and ביכורים are set down by the מזבח. A מה הצד ignores those separate features. It looks only at what both share: they are brought to the holy place and need the בית המקדש. מעשר shares that too.

keyTerms.meaning: An argument built on the common feature of two sources, after each one alone has been knocked down
Let the logical argument come back

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the גמרא is going back to one source alone. A מה הצד uses both sources together, so their separate weak points no longer matter.

phrases.english: But let the logical argument return,
phrases.notes: He means: go back to the logic that failed in steps 3–5 and try it in a new way.

phrases.english: and derive it through 'what they have in common'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions why the פסוק of step 6 was needed when a combined logical argument seems possible
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for the פסוק in step 6
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Each source failed only because of its own unique feature. Their shared feature still applies to מעשר, so logic should be enough.

steps.title: The shared feature of both is a link to the מזבח
steps.stepSummary: The מה הצד fails because בכור and ביכורים both have some link to the מזבח, and מעשר does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because it can be refuted: what about the common feature of the two? They both have some connection to the מזבח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question of step 7. The מה הצד doesn't work, because both sources share something that מעשר lacks.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בכור is offered on the מזבח, and ביכורים are placed next to it. So the two do share a feature, but it is a connection to the מזבח. מעשר has no such connection, so the comparison falls apart, and a פסוק is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: To refute; to knock down an argument
The common feature shared by two sources
Some connection to the מזבח

steps.whatToRemember: A מה הצד fails if the two sources share a further feature that the new case lacks. Here that feature is צד מזבח.

phrases.english: Because it can be refuted:
What about the common feature between them?
They both have an aspect of the altar.
phrases.notes: The blood of the בכור goes on the מזבח, and ביכורים are set down beside it. מעשר has neither.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to a shared feature of both sources that the new case lacks
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A מה הצד from בכור and ביכורים should prove the law of מעשר
steps.terutzMaskana: Both sources share צד מזבח, which מעשר lacks, so the פסוק is needed

steps.title: Which view of the first holiness does רבי ישמעאל hold?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי ישמעאל holds about קדושה ראשונה. Each possible answer seems to cause a problem regarding בכור.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does he hold? If he holds the first holiness worked for its time and for the future, then even a בכור should be allowed today! And if he holds it did not work for the future, then the question should be asked about a בכור too!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the whole comparison by asking which view רבי ישמעאל holds. It sets up two options, and each one runs into a problem with בכור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Option one: if the holiness of the מקדש area still remains, offerings could be brought today, so even a בכור would be allowed. Then בכור cannot be the example of something that needs the בית המקדש. Option two: if the holiness has ended, a בכור should be just as open to question as מעשר. So why treat בכור as the clear example to learn from?

keyTerms.meaning: The first sanctification of the מקדש and ירושלים, from the time of שלמה
It made the place holy for its own time
For the future, even after the חורבן
Let it be a question; it should be in doubt

steps.confusionAlert: This argument has two halves, and each half raises its own problem. Because the two options cover every possibility, the גמרא is showing that either way, בכור seems a bad example to learn from.

phrases.english: What does he hold?
If he holds that the first sanctification
sanctified for its time and sanctified for the future,
then even a firstborn as well should be allowed!

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי קָסָבַר לֹא קִידְּשָׁה לֶעָתִיד לָבֹא –
phrases.english: And if he holds it did not sanctify for the future,
then let the question be raised about a firstborn too!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי קָסָבַר? אִי קָסָבַר קְדוּשָּׁה רִאשׁוֹנָה קִידְּשָׁה לִשְׁעָתָהּ וְקִידְּשָׁה לֶעָתִיד לָבֹא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Steps back from the method of proof and questions the basic idea underneath the comparison to בכור
steps.kashyaTarget: Using בכור as the clear example of something that needs the בית המקדש
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two-option dilemma. If the holiness remains, a בכור is allowed today. If it does not, a בכור is as uncertain as מעשר. Either way, בכור is not a clear source.

steps.title: רבינא: a בכור whose blood was sprinkled before the חורבן
steps.stepSummary: רבינא says רבי ישמעאל holds the holiness did not last. The בכור in question is one whose blood was sprinkled before the חורבן, and its meat still remains.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: Really he holds it did not sanctify for the future. Here we are dealing with a בכור whose blood was sprinkled before the בית המקדש was destroyed. Then the בית המקדש was destroyed, and its meat still exists.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא answers step 9 by choosing the second option. He then explains which kind of בכור רבי ישמעאל was talking about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the holiness ended, nobody could bring a new בכור today. The case being compared is a בכור whose blood was already sprinkled while the בית המקדש stood, and only its meat is left. That case is just about eating meat after the חורבן, so it matches מעשר, which is also only about eating.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, truly; keeping to the original view
What case are we dealing with here?
Its blood was sprinkled on the מזבח
The destruction of the בית המקדש

steps.whatToRemember: רבי ישמעאל holds that קדושה ראשונה did not last for the future. His comparison is to a בכור whose blood was done before the חורבן, so only the eating of its meat is in question, just like מעשר.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how the גמרא saves a comparison by narrowing the example to one exact case. That narrow case lines up with the case being learned.

phrases.english: Ravina said:
Actually, he holds it did not sanctify for the future;
and here, what are we dealing with?
With a firstborn whose blood was sprinkled
before the destruction of the Temple,
and then the Temple was destroyed,
and its meat still exists.
phrases.notes: So the only question left is about eating the meat, which is just like the question about eating מעשר.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבִינָא: לְעוֹלָם קָסָבַר לֹא קִידְּשָׁה; וְהָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the dilemma of step 9 by choosing the second option and narrowing the case of בכור
steps.terutzResolutionType: Picks one option and limits the case (הכא במאי עסקינן)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The comparison seemed to be about any בכור, which made it hard to explain
steps.terutzMaskana: The holiness did not last. The בכור is one whose blood was sprinkled before the חורבן, so only eating its meat is in question, like מעשר

steps.title: The meat of the בכור is tied to its blood, and מעשר learns from בכור
steps.stepSummary: רבינא's answer continues. The בכור's meat is compared to its blood, so the meat needs a מזבח just as the blood does, and מעשר learns this rule from בכור.
steps.simpleTranslation: Its meat was compared to its blood. Just as its blood goes on the מזבח, its meat also needs a מזבח. Then מעשר comes and learns from בכור.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רבינא's answer from the last step. It explains why this בכור's meat cannot be eaten after the חורבן, even though its blood was already sprinkled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק puts the בכור's blood and meat side by side, so they are compared. The blood needs a מזבח, so eating the meat also needs a מזבח. מעשר then gets the same rule from בכור through the פסוק from step 6.

keyTerms.meaning: Was compared through a היקש, meaning two things are placed together in a פסוק
Its meat
Its blood
And learns from

phrases.english: And its meat was compared to its blood;
just as its blood is on the altar,
so too its meat is with the altar;
phrases.notes: He means the meat may be eaten only while there is a מזבח.

phrases.english: and מעשר comes and learns from בכור.
phrases.notes: This uses the פסוק from step 6 that lists מעשר and בכור together.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבינא's answer by giving the source for why the meat cannot be eaten
steps.terutzResolutionType: Case definition backed by a היקש
steps.terutzMaskana: The meat of the בכור depends on a מזבח because it is compared to its blood, and מעשר follows בכור.

steps.title: Can something learned by a היקש go on to teach by another היקש?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects. The בכור's meat got its rule through a היקש, so it should not be able to pass that rule to מעשר through a second היקש.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can something that was learned through a היקש turn around and teach through another היקש?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the chain built in step 11, which goes from blood to meat to מעשר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a rule in קדשים that a law learned from a היקש cannot be passed on through another היקש. The meat learned from the blood by a היקש, and now it is supposed to teach מעשר by another היקש. That looks like exactly what the rule forbids.

keyTerms.meaning: Something whose law was learned from a היקש
Turns around and teaches something else
Holy things, such as קרבנות

phrases.english: But can a matter learned through a היקש
then turn around and teach through a היקש?!
phrases.notes: This is a known rule for קדשים: you cannot stack one היקש on top of another.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי דָּבָר הַלָּמֵד בְּהֶיקֵּשׁ חוֹזֵר וּמְלַמֵּד בְּהֶיקֵּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the chain of learning set up in step 11
steps.kashyaTarget: The derivation blood → meat of בכור → מעשר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In קדשים, a law learned by a היקש may not teach a further case by another היקש.

steps.title: Grain מעשר is not holy in this sense
steps.stepSummary: The answer: grain מעשר counts as חולין, so the rule against stacking היקשים, which is only for קדשים, does not apply.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 12.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban on a היקש teaching through another היקש applies only to קדשים. מעשר שני made of grain counts as חולין for this rule. So the second היקש, which teaches מעשר, is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: מעשר taken from grain
Not holy, ordinary

phrases.english: Grain מעשר is non-holy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא by limiting the rule to קדשים
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of a rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ban on stacking היקשים blocks learning מעשר from בכור.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ban is only for קדשים, and grain מעשר counts as חולין.

steps.title: That answer works for only one opinion
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that this answer only works if we decide by the thing being taught (מעשר). If we decide by the thing doing the teaching (the holy בכור), the problem comes back.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works for the one who says we follow the learner. But for the one who says we follow the teacher, what can we say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer from step 13 and shows it does not satisfy everyone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a dispute over how to decide whether a case counts as קדשים. We can look at the case that learns (here מעשר, which is חולין), or at the case that teaches (here בכור, which is קדשים). For the second opinion, the chain is still forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: This works out fine
We follow the case that learns
We follow the case that teaches
What can be said? (there is a problem)

phrases.english: This works well according to the one who says
we follow the one that learns;
phrases.notes: The one that learns here is מעשר, and the one that teaches is the בכור.

phrases.english: but according to the one who says
we follow the one that teaches –
what is there to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנִיחָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר בָּתַר לָמֵד אָזְלִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the answer in step 13 fits only one side of a dispute
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that grain מעשר is חולין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the teaching case decides the matter, the teacher here is the holy בכור, so the stacking ban applies.

steps.title: Blood and meat count as one thing
steps.stepSummary: Final answer: the blood and the meat of the בכור are one single thing, so the meat never learned from the blood. There is only one היקש, from בכור to מעשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Blood and meat are one thing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives an answer that works for everyone, so it no longer matters which case decides the status.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem only existed because we counted two היקשים: blood to meat, and then meat to מעשר. If blood and meat are one thing, the first step is not a separate היקש. מעשר simply learns from the whole בכור in one step, so nothing is stacked.

keyTerms.meaning: One single matter

steps.whatToRemember: רבי ישמעאל's source holds up: מעשר learns from בכור, and the בכור needs a מזבח. Because blood and meat are one thing, there is no forbidden chain of היקשים.
steps.whyThisMatters: This saves the proof that even קדשים קלים, such as the meat of a בכור, may not be eaten when there is no מזבח. רבין brings this rule to רבי ירמיה in the next step.

phrases.english: Blood and meat are one matter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 14 by showing there was only one היקש all along
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the derivation so the problem disappears
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Meat learned from blood, and then מעשר learned from meat, which would be two stacked היקשים.
steps.terutzMaskana: Blood and meat are one unit, so מעשר learns from בכור in a single היקש.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: מעשר is eaten only when there is a מזבח, learned from בכור without breaking the rule against stacking היקשים.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה mocks the Babylonian teaching
steps.stepSummary: רבין brings the rule (that קדשים קלים need the מזבח) to ארץ ישראל, and רבי ירמיה calls the Babylonians foolish for saying such an unclear teaching.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבין went up to ארץ ישראל, he said this teaching in front of רבי ירמיה. רבי ירמיה said: Foolish Babylonians! Because they live in a dark land, they say dark, unclear teachings!
steps.whatsHappening: The rule we just worked so hard to explain is brought to ארץ ישראל, and רבי ירמיה strongly rejects it. This step sets up his proof, which comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now, the גמרא was defending the idea that קדשים קלים cannot be eaten without a מזבח, learned from בכור. Now a major אמורא from ארץ ישראל says the whole rule is wrong. He has not yet given his reason. That comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: When he went up (from בבל to ארץ ישראל)
A teaching or ruling
Foolish Babylonians
Dark, meaning unclear or mistaken

phrases.english: When Ravin went up,
he said this teaching in front of Rabbi Yirmeya.
phrases.notes: "This teaching" is the rule from before: even lighter sacrifices can't be eaten when the מזבח is missing.

phrases.english: He said: Foolish Babylonians!
Because they live in a dark land,
they say dark teachings!
phrases.notes: He's making a wordplay: a "dark" land produces "dark" teachings, meaning unclear ones.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי סְלֵיק רָבִין, אַמְרַהּ לִשְׁמַעְתָּא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יִרְמְיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from defending how the rule is learned to an outright rejection of the rule itself.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole rule that קדשים קלים cannot be eaten without a מזבח.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Not stated yet. רבי ירמיה only calls the teaching unclear here, and his proof follows.

steps.title: First source: sacrifices become disqualified during the journeys
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה quotes a ברייתא saying that when the משכן was taken down for travel, קדשים became פסול, while זבים and מצורעים were still sent out of their camps.
steps.simpleTranslation: Haven't they heard what a ברייתא teaches? When the משכן was taken down for the journeys, sacrifices became disqualified, and זבים and מצורעים were still sent outside their boundary.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה starts building his proof by quoting the first of two ברייתות. On its own, this one seems to agree with the Babylonian rule, so wait for the second source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the משכן was packed up, the מזבח was not standing, and this ברייתא says קדשים became פסול then. It also says the camp boundaries still applied for זבים and מצורעים. This source is half of a contradiction that the next step will resolve.

keyTerms.meaning: Haven't they heard?
Taking the משכן down for the journeys
Become disqualified
People with a זיבה flow and people with צרעת
Boundary of a camp

phrases.english: Haven't they heard what is taught in a baraita:
At the time of taking down for the journeys
sacrifices become disqualified,
and zavim and lepers
are sent outside the boundary;
phrases.notes: Even while traveling, the camp boundaries still counted, so these people still had to stay outside.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins supplying the evidence for רבי ירמיה's rejection.
steps.raayaObject: Part of the proof that קדשים קלים do not need a standing מזבח.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about the time of סילוק מסעות.

steps.title: Second source and the proof: lighter sacrifices could still be eaten
steps.stepSummary: A second ברייתא says קדשים were eaten in two places. רבי ירמיה settles the conflict by saying the first ברייתא speaks about קדשי קדשים and the second about קדשים קלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another ברייתא teaches: sacrifices are eaten in two places. Isn't it clear that the first ברייתא speaks about קדשי קדשים and the second speaks about קדשים קלים?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה brings a second ברייתא that seems to contradict the first. He settles the contradiction in a way that proves the Babylonian rule wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One source says קדשים became פסול during travel, and the other says they could still be eaten. If the first means קדשי קדשים and the second means קדשים קלים, then קדשים קלים could be eaten even with no standing מזבח. That directly breaks the rule learned from בכור.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it not that? (a proof formula)
Most-holy sacrifices
Sacrifices of lighter holiness

steps.whyThisMatters: If this proof stands, the whole line of reasoning in steps 11 to 15 would be defending a rule that is simply false.

phrases.english: And another baraita teaches:
Sacrifices are eaten in two places.
phrases.notes: He means they could be eaten both where the משכן stood and later, while it was being carried.

phrases.english: What, is it not that
this one is about the most holy sacrifices,
and that one is about lighter sacrifices?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתַנְיָא אִידַּךְ: בִּשְׁנֵי מְקוֹמוֹת קֳדָשִׁים נֶאֱכָלִים. מַאי, לָאו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the proof by adding the second ברייתא and settling the conflict between the two.
steps.raayaObject: קדשים קלים may be eaten even when the מזבח is not standing.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Two ברייתות about the מדבר journeys, read as speaking about two different levels of holiness.

steps.title: רבינא: both sources are about lighter sacrifices
steps.stepSummary: רבינא rejects רבי ירמיה's reading and says both ברייתות speak about קדשים קלים. He promises a different way to settle them, which comes on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: Both ברייתות are speaking about קדשים קלים, and there is no contradiction.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא pushes back on רבי ירמיה's proof by saying both ברייתות are about the same kind of sacrifice. This is a setup line, and his actual explanation comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ירמיה's proof depended on splitting the ברייתות between two levels of holiness. רבינא takes that split away, which means the contradiction must be settled some other way. That way could keep the rule that קדשים קלים need the מזבח.

keyTerms.meaning: Both this one and that one
And it is not difficult (there is no contradiction)

steps.confusionAlert: רבינא has not finished his answer yet. The words "it is not difficult" lead into his explanation, which comes right after this.

phrases.english: Ravina said:
Both this and that are about lighter sacrifices;
and it is not difficult –

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבִינָא: אִידֵּי וְאִידֵּי בְּקָדָשִׁים קַלִּים; וְלָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the way רבי ירמיה divided the two ברייתות.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רבי ירמיה's reading that the two ברייתות speak about different levels of holiness.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Both ברייתות can be read as speaking about קדשים קלים, so the proof does not hold. The way to settle them follows next.
